transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SA), Alex (CTO, Sable), Dana (Lead ML Eng), Samir (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery to map Sable's inference needs for a potential pilot. Main areas: open model comparison (LLM choices), context length needs (long docs & chat), multilingual support, tool-calling / function calling for internal systems, and VPC/private deployment constraints. Customer wants cost vs latency tradeoffs and a security-package before committing to a POC.

Topics: - Model selection (open models vs variants)
- Context length / KV cache behavior
- Multilingual evaluation (EN + ES + FR)
- Tool-calling / function calling for DB lookups and internal tooling
- Deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Benchmarking next steps

Action items (recap in call body): see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah, uh we're excited to chat through your inference needs. I'm Jordan, account lead. Priya and Marcus from our solutions team are with me. Could we do quick intros?
[00:08] Alex: Alex here, CTO at Sable. Dana's my lead on the ML side, Samir on product. We're evaluating where to run inference for two main products — a conversational support bot and a doc-summarization pipeline.
[00:18] Dana: hi all. Our big constraints are cost — we need under a certain per-call budget — and we also have some strict data residency and audit requirements.
[00:25] Priya: got it. One quick question to calibrate: are you leaning towards open models only or do you consider managed LLMs?
[00:32] Alex: Open models: prefer open-source for cost and control, but if hosted managed gives easier ops and SLA that could be interesting. We care about latency under 200ms 95th for chat in the support use case. The summarization job can be higher latency.
[00:46] Marcus: 200ms P95 is pretty aggressive for hosted, depends on model size and sequence length. We can discuss trade-offs: smaller quantized variants on Dedicated can hit low-latency whereas Hosted with larger context will have higher median.
[00:58] Dana: our chat has context windows around 2k tokens typically, but some support agents paste long transcripts — up to 8k in worst case. For summarization we supply full docs up to 32k. Multi-lingual: ~20% Spanish, 5% French, rest English. And we need function-calling to run DB lookups and initiate internal ticket creation.
[01:18] Jordan: good, that clarifies. So the big questions for model selection are: context length capability (8k vs 32k), multilingual fidelity, and tool/function-calling support. And deployment mode because of data residency and KMS requirements.
[01:30] Samir: yes and also the audit logs / retention. We have compliance needs: SOC 2, ISO certs, and we manage keys so KMS integration or customer HSM is a must.
[01:38] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; Dedicated offers isolated capacity with better latency consistency, and Hosted is the fastest path to ramp but has managed keys unless you go with a bring-your-own-key option for some customers. Quick call-out: sometimes bring-your-own-key on Hosted has limits — we can send the specifics in the security pack.
[01:56] Alex: that's helpful. On models, what open model families do you recommend for doc summarization at 32k? We're looking at Llama-3-70B-32k variants and some Mistral/Redwood verified builds.
[02:08] Marcus: for 32k you want a variant with explicit long-context training/position-embedding handling. Llama-3 70B 32k can work but you pay on tokens and latency. Mistral long-context forks can be efficient. There are also retriever+chunking patterns — e.g., hybrid retrieval so you only pass relevant chunks to a shorter context model for summarization. That can save cost.
[02:26] Dana: hmm, we considered retrieval augmentation but worry about semantic drift and the need to keep the model aware of full document for coherence. Does Redwood offer prefix/KV cache to handle repeated context across users?
[02:36] Priya: yes, we have automatic prefix cache and KV caching for streaming chat sessions. For the support bot we can keep per-conversation KV in memory and reuse across rapid back-and-forth to reduce recomputation. That works well for both Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports caching too but deduplication windows differ.
[02:54] Alex: any quantization recommendations? We're running on fairly tight hardware budgets.
[02:58] Marcus: 4-bit quantization (LLM.int8/4 variants) often offers the best cost/latency sweet spot, but watch quality on instruction-following tasks. For multilingual we usually test quantized variants against your prompts — there's some degradation in low-resource languages. We can include quantization A/B notes in the perf run.
[03:16] Samir: about function-calling — we need deterministic structured responses (JSON payloads) so our orchestration can parse and invoke APIs. How mature is Redwood's function-calling / tool-calling surface for open models?
[03:26] Priya: we support function/tool calling on our API with a structured schema. For open models, we map calls via a shim that extracts JSON-like responses and validates them. For model variants without native function-calling support, we do a post-processing step with strong assertions and a small verifier. It works in production for many customers but sometimes requires patterns to coax reliable outputs.
[03:42] Dana: any examples of customers using tool-calling for internal DB queries? I need to understand latency implications — if every call is making a DB lookup, that could increase end-to-end SLOs.
[03:50] Jordan: good point. Many setups use a synchronous verification pattern: model emits a function call indicating which record to fetch, the infra fetches it and returns to model for finalization. That doubles round trips in worst case. To mitigate we suggest: pre-fetching likely data, local caches, and async ticket creation where possible. Also Redwood routing can send heavy tool-calls to Dedicated pools with reserved throughput.
[04:09] Alex: are we able to pin model versions during rollouts? We need to A/B test a new open-model build before shifting production traffic.
[04:16] Marcus: yes, Redwood supports model version pinning and canary / A/B rollouts with automatic fallback. That works across Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments it depends on your upgrade policy but the control plane supports rollout configs.
[04:29] Samir: cost question — if we keep conversations around 2k tokens with occasional 8k and summarization 32k, ballpark monthly cost? We have 200k chats/month and 10k summarization jobs.
[04:39] Marcus: rough back-of-envelope: chat usage with a compact 13B quantized model on Dedicated might be X $/k tokens; summarization using a 70B 32k variant will be more. We'll send an itemized estimate. The important lever is routing: use smaller models for chat where quality is okay, and large for summarization. Also caching and retrieval will reduce token counts.
[04:58] [Speaker 1]: (inaudible) ...we also have regulatory nodes in EU — any residency problems?
[05:03] Priya: Redwood Dedicated can be provisioned in region-specific clusters. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the recommended for strict residency. Hosted has multi-region endpoints but some customers prefer Dedicated for SLA+residency.
[05:16] Dana: about benchmarks — can we run a Redwood-hosted perf test using our sample prompts and our latency SLO? We could provide representative traffic.
[05:23] Jordan: absolutely. Priya and Marcus will run a 1-hour profiling run with your prompt set and two model candidates (a 13B quantized and a 70B long-context). We'll measure median and p95 latencies, token cost, and top-level quality signals.
[05:34] Priya: when you share prompts please include tokenization distribution — it helps pick optimal chunk sizes and batching configs. Also include language labels so we can test ES/FR quality.
[05:43] Alex: we'll share a small set today and the token distribution by Friday. About SSO and admin access — we use SAML and fine-grained RBAC, can Redwood integrate?
[05:50] Marcus: yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC roles. For Dedicated/Private we can sync to your IDP; for Hosted we also have SSO options with SCIM provisioning.
[06:00] Dana: curious about model updates — if we run a Dedicated cluster with pinned model, how disruptive are model pulls? We can't afford long maintenance windows.
[06:07] Priya: Dedicated supports rolling model updates with canary traffic. Kernel-level warmup is the main time sink — we can pre-warm GPUs and do staged swaps to keep disruption minimal. We'll share typical maintenance timelines.
[06:19] Samir: one final: for multilingual, do you recommend multilingual models or separate per-language fine-tuned models?
[06:26] Marcus: trade-offs: single multilingual model is operationally simpler but may underperform in niche languages. If Spanish is a big portion, a Spanish-optimized model can improve quality. For your distribution (20% ES, 5% FR), I'd recommend testing a multilingual baseline and a Spanish-specialized model for chat test bucket. We'll include a quality delta in the perf run.
[06:45] [00:06:45] Alex: (overlap) ok let's talk security specifics post-call, send the SOC2 excerpts and KMS architecture doc.
[06:53] Jordan: will do. We'll also include notes on BYOK limitations on Hosted.
[06:58] [Speaker 2]: small audio hiccup, sorry.
[07:02] Priya: quick technical note on KV caching and streaming: if you're doing streaming responses while updating the KV cache, we ensure eventual consistency for mid-turn updates — there are patterns to minimize stale context, we can walk through those in the technical deep-dive.
[07:18] Dana: perfect, we probably need a follow-up SE deep dive focused on caching + function-calls and the end-to-end latency impact.
[07:25] Jordan: propose two follow-ups: 1) 1-hour perf test (Practical) where we run your prompts against two candidate setups; 2) SE-led deep dive on caching and tool-calling (technical). Good to schedule next week?
[07:37] Alex: yes next week works. Dana and I will align on windows.
[07:41] Samir: timeline question — internal timeline is to decide on a pilot by end of July and go into a paid pilot in early Aug if results look good.
[07:49] Jordan: noted. We'll prioritize the perf run and get security docs today.
[07:54] Marcus: quick competitor note — a few customers have tried Anthropic/GPT-like endpoints; they offer good instruction following but cost is an issue compared to optimized open models on Dedicated. We'll include a short comparison in the follow-up.
[08:07] Dana: any gotchas we should watch for in prompt engineering for long-context summarization?
[08:12] Priya: chunking strategy, system prompt clarity, and chunk-overlap heuristics matter. Also consider progressive summarization (summarize chunks then summarize summaries) to control tokens. We'll send example recipes.
[08:23] Alex: great. That covers my main concerns. Thanks everyone.

Recap (end of call):
- Redwood to send security pack (SOC2 excerpts, BYOK notes, KMS integration details).
- SEs to run perf test with sample prompts: 13B-quantized vs 70B-long-context. Measure median/p95 and token cost.
- Customer to provide prompt set, token distribution and targets by July 16.
- Schedule deep-dive on KV caching + function-calling implementation.

End of recording.
